newsitem.title: USA: Millennium sees Tioxide deal as possibility.
newsitem.headline: Millennium sees Tioxide deal as possibility.

text.p: Millennium Chemicals Inc on Friday said it saw no antitrust barriers to prevent it from striking a deal with Tioxide, which is being spun off from Britain's Imperial Chemical Industries Plc in the next year to 18 months.

Tioxide and Millennium both manufacture titanium dioxide, which is used in pigments. That business suffers from low prices and inefficient capacity, which analysts and companies believe could be alleviated by mergers and consolidation.

"We do not see any reasons why we should be excluded. They have no presence in the U.S. apart from a joint venture," Millennium President Robert Lee said after the release of the company's first-quarter results. He was responding to an analyst's question on whether the two companies could strike some kind of merger or acquisition deal.
Millennium said overcapacity was still plaguing the industry, but it expected the industry would be forced to close production facilities and some players would exit the business.
"Many people will be faced with capital decisions. People are cannibalizing lines for plants and maintenance," Lee said.
Millennium said operating rates in the industry would improve to the low- to mid-90 percent range by 1999 from the high 80 percent range recently.
"The industry as a whole wants consolidation," said Lee.
